quest.title: Sacrificial Offering
quest.description: According to Hanachirusato, these barriers must be broken to cleanse the Thunder Sakura's roots. The next barrier seems to be located in the abandoned shrine to the northeast of Konda Village. Although the place sounds quite unsettling indeed, this is Hanachirusato's request, so it is best that you see it done.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A fox statue... Yup, it's the same as the one in Konda Village!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon doesn't see a ward in it... or has the ward been hidden?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, it's some troublesome <color=#00E1FFFF>secret</color> again, isn't it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, right? The village chief told us everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! There's some writing here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>"The ward has been sealed within by sacred words."</color>

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, what does that mean? There's some more writing here as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Although I hope the seal will never be broken, and although you have now been missing for many years... If the seal must be broken and the Cleansing Ritual conducted, I hope that you shall be the one to break it."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The third line of the sacred words is something you often used to say in the past."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... "But if the one to undo the seal is my successor, then there is one extra step you must go through."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "There are four great spirits, and three spokes in the Mitsudomoe. I have placed <color=#00E1FFFF>three shikigami</color> here as guardians. <color=#00E1FFFF>Only when they are all gathered here in one place</color> can you proceed."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "I wouldn't call this layer of security all that useful, but it should still serve to fend off some petty thieves."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is it, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we have to find a solution!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Otherwise, we'd be no better than "petty thieves"!

choices.text: I sure hope that isn't the case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that should do it! Phew, Paimon's exhausted!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shouldn't I be the exhausted one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's not fuss over the details, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, looks like there's a book in here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's so hard to read!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's read it all, but it also feels like Paimon didn't read anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Forget it. Let's get some professional help!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since it's about gods and demons and stuff, let's go to the Grand Narukami Shrine, shall we?

talks.objective: Go to the abandoned shrine northeast of Konda Village

talks.objective: Carry out the investigation at the abandoned shrine

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: The use of sacred words was said to have become a lost art after the Kamuna bloodline failed...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: ...Ah, sorry, I didn't see you there. The Memento Lens is yours to keep. Take it out to see the world, would you?

talks.objective: Continue the investigation at the abandoned shrine

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler from afar. Welcome to the Grand Narukami Shrine!

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: If you have some trouble or just want to make a wish, feel free to ask Ms. Gendou for a fortune slip. May the Electro Archon bless you.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I see. I understand the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a very important rite, and there are indeed records of it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: But the actual details of the ritual have been lost. The Summary you are holding is a very valuable historical artifact in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lost?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are the Fatui behind this? If you say it's so important, then they might be up to something here too...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Oh no. The degradation here is due to poor preservation, humidity, and moths.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's a great shame, but a lot of historical records have been lost. Lady Yae and Sir Kamisato were fretting over this earlier as well.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: But as for the sacred words, I do know a thing or two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! Please tell us how to unseal that ward!

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I apologize, but the sacred words used to seal the ward are not some sort of specific formula.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: ... Instead, they are something created by the one who casts the seal themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What do you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The spell... was created on the fly by the caster?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: This is not precisely so, either. Sacred words of this sort do have some rules.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do elaborate.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Hmm... I believe that the records go something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: The first line represents one's own status in Inazuma. Something with the word "envoy" attached to it, I believe...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: The second line is meant to explain the source of one's power. Something like dango, ramen, or a light novel, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it. Those are definitely great power sources!

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I'm just giving an example. The records use something like "Onmyou Hakkyou."

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: As for the third line...

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Yes, you've guessed it. It can be whatever you want it to be.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Considering how long it's been, I doubt that any still live who understand how to use this third line.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, what shall we do, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden's commission... and this whole nation... it's all gonna go kaput!

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Mm. Perhaps these two items can be of aid to you.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: This is the <color=#00E1FFFF>Memento Lens</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Memento? So it's a souvenir?

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Since the two of you are so knowledgeable, I trust that you must have heard of the Kamera? It's a Fontaine-made device that can record images.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: A long time ago, when Ritou was first founded, the Hiiragi Clan leader Hiroshi imported many new inventions from other places to prove the benefits of building a trading hub.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: For example, he used a Snezhnayan blast furnace to turn an old Hiiragi Clan mansion at Tenshukaku into a hot spring, before sending it as a gift and token of appreciation to Her Excellency.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: He also used the demon-exorcising mirror gifted to the Hiiragi Clan by the Kitsune Saiguu to create a special Kamera in Fontaine. It can record thoughts and memories. It was returned to us here at the Shrine as a token of appreciation and friendship.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: As the years passed, the Kamera itself ceased to function. Only the lens blessed by the Kitsune Saiguu can still see things that no longer exist in certain special places.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: We extracted the lens and named it the Memento Lens.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: The two of you have come on account of the "sakura," and I can sense from our conversation that you are trustworthy.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: I believe that it will come to good use in your hands.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Such an important item...

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: I suppose you may not be familiar with this as outsiders, but we believe that everything has a soul. Even stones and trees have memories! And when an item is left unused for a long time, it will grow bitter with dissatisfaction.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: As such, we might as well give the Lens to someone who can show it all the changes the world has gone through rather than letting it gather dust in our shrine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem! Leave it to us!

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Legend has it that after the Kitsune Saiguu disappeared, her familiars, the <color=#00E1FFFF>Earth Kitsune</color> of Narukami Island, turned into sleeping statues in many places, waiting for her to return.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: If you see a small, strange-looking fox statue, looking at it through the <color=#00E1FFFF>Memento Lens</color> may reveal something new.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: May the Electro Archon bless you! I shall be counting on you two, then.

choices.text: Is it something you can just make up?

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Hmm. Yes, it looks like the spirit veins here can still be used.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Her familiars are also here. Yes, it is a fine place.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Well then, allow me to use sacred words to protect this ward.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Then the first line shall be <color=#00E1FFFF>"In the name of Narukami's envoy."</color>

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: ...Guess I'll just follow the previous example and use <color=#00E1FFFF>"And of the Hakushin bloodline."</color> as the second line. I am no master onmyouji, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: You are... that person who seems very nice on the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Hey, long time no see. Guess you're still so cold to me, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: ...Wait, no. Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: This scent... Is it time for the Cleansing Ritual again?

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: I am... Call me "Hanachirusato."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: ...No need to tell me. I get it.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: I thought she had returned for a moment there... Huh, so that's what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't worry about it. Nice to meet you, Miss Hanachirusato!

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: I... I remember now. About the Sacred Sakura. About you. About Raiden.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Ah, wait. Perhaps what you're seeing right now is not me, but Ioroi in disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: After all, Miss Hanachirusato, you've never seen me in person before, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: I'm not sure there would be much difference either way, if my memory serves.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Eh? Come on, that was uncalled for...

talks.objective: Head to the Grand Narukami Shrine to investigate
Return to the abandoned shrine and use the Memento Lens to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: How quickly the shrine has fallen to neglect after losing its master and the incense within...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: I can only hope that the barrier within the cavern still stands strong.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: Ah, I remember now. She once instructed people to <color=#00E1FFFF>construct a locked gate</color> by a canal on the road leading to Chinju Forest, before giving the key to the Konda Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: I hope everything is still alright.

talks.objective: Recite the sacred words in front of the Sky Kitsune Statue

dialogues.speaker: Records
dialogues.text: "The ward has been sealed in place using <color=#00E1FFFF>sacred words</color>. There are four great spirits, and three spokes in the Mitsudomoe. I have placed <color=#00E1FFFF>three shikigami</color> here as guardians. <color=#00E1FFFF>Only when they are all gathered here in one place</color> can one proceed."

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: Again, the two of you have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This again, eh...

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: I apologize. There are some things that become... a habit, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you following us again? Couldn't you just say hello?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, um, sorry. Paimon's tired from floating around too much... Paimon didn't mean to be rude.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: It is alright. The barrier here has been undone successfully, and thus does the Cleansing Ritual come a step closer to completion. Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's the deal with the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual, anyway? Is it the same as the "cleansing" you asked us to do earlier?

choices.text: Miss Inagi also mentioned this before...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Inagi? Is Miss Inagi a shrine maiden named Misato, by any chance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Her name is Hotomi, Paimon thinks.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Ah, that's right. It has been such a long time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she also said that the method has been lost.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Ah. Hmm... Well, it has been so long, after all...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: It is understandable. I mean, so much time has passed. Don't worry, I'm not angry. Yes, it's just my memory throwing a tantrum.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden does seem to be very angry, actually...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...Anyway, the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a rite of purification.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The Thunder Sakura of Narukami Island can absorb the filth within the earth. But over time, that filth will accumulate.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: If too much filth accumulates, the Thunder Sakura may wither.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Therefore, it is necessary to perform some "minor purifications" on the roots of Thunder Sakura scattered in five places around Narukami Island every once in a while, and to set a barrier up. This way, they are given the power to remove the accumulated filth.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the Cleansing Ritual, then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: When there is enough filth accumulated in the barrier, it becomes necessary to perform the Cleansing Ritual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, Paimon gets it! So, when performing the Cleansing Ritual, we'll need to use a ward to break the barrier over the tree roots.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: This is an excellent understanding of the situation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! We've done it twice now, after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, those monsters that looked like samurai were...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: So, is that how they present themselves nowadays...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: They are the embodiment of the land's defilement. Once driven out of the roots by the ward, they will condense into a physical form.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Back then... Uh, I mean, according to past records, they would turn into kasha, inugami, black jades, umibouzu, raging flames, and other such things. And not all of them would harm people, either. For example, there were the tofu boys...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kasha? Tofu boys? What in the world are those?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Oh, people don't know about these creatures nowadays?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: But now, they have all turned into ferocious ochimusha... What has happened to Inazuma?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, so, what if the cleansing rituals aren't performed and the trees do wither?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: As I recall... I mean, the records say that the Thunder Sakura almost withered several hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Monsters raged unchecked then. Even the seas turned black. The Thunder Sakura tried their hardest to absorb all the evil and the filth, and they almost died in the process.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What happened then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The things that came after... I'm really sorry, but I'm not too familiar with them.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Either way, the present situation tells me that the problem was resolved in the end. Someone performed the Cleansing Ritual.

choices.text: You mentioned that there are five places...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Thanks to your efforts, two root barriers have been undone. Next...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Having done and seen so much, the two of you must be tired and hungry. I have prepared some dishes. I hope you will like them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, it looks delicious! You might be wearing a mask, but you're the best shrine maiden in Inazuma for sure!

choices.text: Hooray for the best shrine maiden in the land!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Well then, please enjoy yourself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, this is great!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, now that Paimon thinks about it, we just ate so much, but it feels like we've eaten nothing at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden, did you...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: How could you suggest that I would do such a thing?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Regardless, please don't worry. These dishes were made with magic I secretly learned from the bake-danuki. They are absolutely harmless. Generally speaking.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The reason I have served you such suspicious... Well, delicious food, is to help heal the remaining roots.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The Chinju Forest is also home to a ward and a root that requires cleansing. And I believe that an old friend of mine still dwells deep within that forest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "You believe"?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: It was a very long time ago. I'm afraid that I'm not entirely sure if he remembers me. Or if he might hate me.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: He can't move freely, and he can't communicate with people, either. But after eating this, you should be able to communicate with him.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: That old friend of mine should be able to help you at least a little. So I did this, for the sake of the Cleansing Ritual.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The two of you have already twice demonstrated your honor, compassion, and skill.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Surely, you will finish this deed for the sake of this land's well-being, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Since Miss Masked Maiden says we have to, let's finish this fight!

choices.text: Are you two teaming up to tease me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! How could you say that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the other roots?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Apart from Chinju Forest, there is a tree root at a place called Araumi.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I wonder if there are still people living there. I haven't been there for a long time.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The last one... is outside the Kamisato residence. There is a pit on a beach northeast of there, and the root is within.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I leave the Cleansing Ritual to you...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Please go ahead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Back there in the abandoned shrine, Miss Masked Maiden, we saw someone who looked just like you through the Memento Lens...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Her name was "Hanachirusato." Are you that Hanachirusato?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Indeed I am.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Has Paimon been cheated?

choices.text: She said so in the beginning, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, anyway, what was that all about?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I'm sorry. I never meant to hide anything from you. I've just never had a chance to explain.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Nor is now the right time either. I'm really sorry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Fine, Paimon gets it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just let us know once you've got the chance, Miss Masked Maiden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right? {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Ah yes. One other thing. When you spoke of the "Memento Lens" earlier, what were you referring to...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...Th—That mirror, Hiroshi... He...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wh—What happened?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...*sigh*

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I lost my composure. Please forgive me. In that case, please keep this "Memento Lens" safe. It is a very precious instrument indeed.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Please do! It is very precious!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I'll be sure to look after it well...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: There are small fox statues in many different places. They are called Earth Kitsune. With the Memento Lens, one can summon forth scenes from the past at those statues' locations.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: If it can be of aid in your adventures, please make good use of the Memento Lens.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll use it well!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Please do, and protect it! Don't bump it against things, and remember to clean it regularly!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, got it!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: That's good. Now then, if you'll excuse me, I must go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How will we meet up?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "If the crimson sakura knows the pain of parting, it will forever stay."

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Our fates shall surely be entwined like those of the Sakura Bloom.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Till our next meeting, I will be praying for your success beneath the well in Konda Village, where you successfully purified the Thunder Sakura root. I wish you all the best.

choices.text: I'll keep it safe, trust me.
You're the only one who's been calling her "Miss Masked Maiden"...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: You seem very sensitive to things of a mystical nature.

choices.text: It seems just a little bit off...
So, we found this book called the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Summary...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Which Paimon didn't understand at all!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: People can't read it nowadays? But it was written in the common tongue...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "People nowadays"? Hey, just how old are you?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Wha— H—Hey, that's very rude of you!

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: ... Yeah, it's decided. We'll let her go this time.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: After all, it's not my job, and it's not as if she is some monster, charging at me like an Ochimusha might.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: I'm all tuckered out already. I thought I had run into a long-lost friend. That feeling is so exhausting...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: Then let us part ways here.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Ah, you're so cold.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: "Rosy-cheeked in the morning, bleached bones by dusk."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Oh, come on! It was at least half an emotional reunion for me! Actually, maybe it was more like one quarter?

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Ah, you're gone already? Come on...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: That being said, after she left, Ioroi seems to have led his tribe to wreak havoc everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Well, I could have kept one eye shut, had Ioroi stayed in the Chinju Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Mm. Guess he needs to be taught a good lesson...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: My, that lady is such a buzzkill.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: If I am to have a disciple one day, I shall find a cheerful and beautiful lady. Yeah, I'll make sure of that.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Now, as for the third line... Ah, right, this looks good.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>"Bring forth the fried tofu"</color>!

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Since this is her territory — the land of the Hakushin bloodline — we'll go with that.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: This was... my previous...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: Wait, that wasn't me. It was her previous territory.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Woman
dialogues.text: That person over there... seems so familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Yeah, guess we're done here. Time to write all this down and hand it over to the shrine.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: After all, this isn't like the shikigami paper I use. With any luck, they'll preserve it properly. Things might get dicey if these document come across moths or water.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Man
dialogues.text: Ah! Silly me, saying such inauspicious things...
